statement: Build a one-file website for CityCare Hospital in Bengaluru where patients can request a visit and find emergency information.
audience: Patients of CityCare Hospital in Bengaluru, including people looking for emergency information.
standards: Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript in one file; CDN libraries allowed; no build step.
Emergency information is easy to find and readable at a glance.
No invented hospital facts: phone numbers, address and ER hours are clearly marked placeholders until the Requester confirms them.
Public emergency numbers 112 (general) and 108 (ambulance) are shown, with Audit verifying them.
The booking form collects only name, phone, department and preferred date/time, and nothing else.
Nothing entered in the form is stored or sent from the page.
A short privacy notice is shown with the form.
rules: Booking is a 'Request a visit' form, not a slot picker; no availability is shown.
After submit, the confirmation states that the hospital will call to confirm; it never implies a held appointment.
Do not ask for symptoms or medical history.
Do not invent CityCare phone numbers, address or ER hours.
Mark the form as a demo that needs a real backend and consent handling before it takes live requests.
done_when: The site is a single HTML file that opens and works with no build step.
A 'Request a visit' form with name, phone, department and preferred date/time shows a confirmation that the hospital will call to confirm.
The form collects no symptoms or history, stores nothing and sends nothing, and a short privacy notice is visible.
An emergency section shows 112 (general) and 108 (ambulance), and Audit has verified both.
All CityCare-specific details (phone, address, ER hours) are either clearly marked placeholders or replaced with details confirmed by the Requester.
Before launch, the Requester has confirmed the real phone numbers, address and ER hours, and the site shows them.
Audit has checked the site against these standards and rules and found no open material defect.
